name: Ada

wants.text: Tin enough to finish the season
Her daughter to learn the trade properly

contradiction: She is proud of work she considers invisible.

provenance.notes: An invented smith. Copper and bronze working on Cyprus is attested. A woman running a bronze workshop is unusual in the surviving evidence but not excluded; she is written as a plausible local case, and the art and dialogue agree that the smith is Ada, with her daughter sorting charcoal.

voice.register: Blunt, technical, talks to the metal. Affection arrives as instruction.
tics: weighing tin in her hand before the scale
watching the color of the coals
avoid: saying the girl’s name in front of strangers
sampleLines: Put it on the scale. Do not tell me it is good; the scale decides.
The good blades go to men who will use them and never think of me.
She has the hands. She does not yet have the patience.
